newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Refinery workers threaten strike in Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Refinery workers threaten strike in Portugal.

text.p: Eighty six workers at Portugal's Sines refinery have told state oil firm Petrogal they planned to strike for three days from October 29 to press for upgrades in their careers and better wages, a company spokesman said.
"Negotiations are continuing. We think the strike will not happen. We are seeking a solution," Antonio Mocho told Reuters.
He said the workers, who help to maintain the external sides of equipment and to process raw material supplies, could not paralyse refinery output but could disrupt production.

Petrogal's 210,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery at Sines in southwestern Portugal expects to resume full production next Monday after a shutdown for maintenance from September 11 to October 21, Mocho said.

The refinery supplies around 60 percent of Portugal's fuel needs and normally exports 90,000 tonnes of gasoline, 30,000 tonnes of jet fuel and 25,000 tonnes of gas oil on the spot market per month, over and above its term contract commitments.
It has a storage capacity of 2.8 million cubic metres, including 1.5 million cubic metres for crude oil.
Portugal's other refinery at Oporto was not affected by the threatened strike, Mocho said.
